title: Fire Safety & Evacuation Guide
summary: Smoke inhalation is the primary hazard in fires. Stay low, get out fast, and never go back inside a burning building.
precautions: Test closed doors with the back of your hand before opening. If hot, do NOT open; use an alternate exit.
Crawl low under smoke where air is cleaner and cooler.
Know at least two fire exit routes from every room in your building.
If your clothes catch fire: STOP, DROP, and ROLL until flames are extinguished.
Install and maintain smoke detectors and ABC dry chemical fire extinguishers on every floor.
evacuation: Evacuate immediately via fire stairwells. Do NOT use elevators under any circumstances.
Close doors behind you as you exit to slow down the spread of fire and smoke.
Proceed to the designated assembly area outside and remain there.
Call Emergency Fire Services (101) as soon as you are safely outside.
firstAid: Cool thermal burns with cool (not icy) running water for 10-15 minutes.
Cover burn areas with clean, non-stick sterile bandages or plastic cling wrap.
Do NOT pop burn blisters or apply butter, oil, or ointments to deep burns.
If smoke inhalation occurs, move victim to fresh air immediately and administer oxygen if available.
emergencyChecklist: Burn gel and sterile gauze dressings
Emergency contact list with Fire Department number (101)
dos: DO stay low to the floor where air is fresher.
DO Stop, Drop, and Roll if clothing catches fire.
DO feel doors for heat before opening.
DO get out immediately and stay out.
donts: DON'T use elevators during a fire.
DON'T re-enter a burning building for belongings.
DON'T inhale smoke; cover your nose with a wet cloth.
